data.gender_notes: Manav is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manav is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘manava’, meaning ‘man’ or ‘human being’. In Hindu mythology, Manav is considered to be the collective term for all humans. This name symbolizes the essence of humanity and our connection to the universe. The name Manav carries the meaning “Man, human being” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manav usually hope their child will grow to embody man, human being and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In Hinduism, humans are believed to be the bridge between the material and spiritual worlds. The name Manav serves as a constant reminder of our spiritual potential and our duty to strive for spiritual growth and enlightenment. vedic_reference.note: Manav is a common name in Hinduism and appears in various religious texts such as the Mahabharata and the Ramayana. It is also mentioned in the Vedas, particularly the Rigveda, where it is used to refer to the human race.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Manav was a sage who is mentioned in several Puranas. He is believed to have been the father of Manavarshi, the first human being. This legend is associated with the creation of mankind and the beginning of human civilization.

historical_references.reference: Manav was also a revered sage and a Lawgiver in ancient India. Manu Smriti, a major legal text in Hinduism, is attributed to him. It is believed to have been composed around 200 BCE.
